title: A file with two names
question: linkat gives a file a second name. Then removing the first: is the file gone?
text: A name is not the file. The file is its inode; a directory entry is a name that points to it, and an inode can have several.

1. [vfs_link](1:vfs_link), then ext4's [__ext4_link](1:__ext4_link): [inc_nlink](1:inc_nlink) counts the inode's names, from 1 to 2, and [__ext4_add_entry](1:__ext4_add_entry) writes "also.txt" into /mnt's directory block, with the same inode number; [d_instantiate](1:d_instantiate) points the new name's dentry at the same inode.

2. Removing the first name: [ext4_delete_entry](2:ext4_delete_entry) takes "note.txt" out of the directory, and [drop_nlink](2:drop_nlink) counts the names down, from 2 to 1: [what it changed](2:drop_nlink:objects). The inode stays: it still has a name. A file goes only when its last name does, as the next lesson shows.
Try: [read it by its new name](try:1): the same bytes, "hello from the disk".
